g.text: require size 1..20 MiB and safe filename
delete(attachment_id) if an object may exist
set bounded error_code in active detail
set size_bytes and SHA-256 in active detail
claim short scan lease in active detail
using retry time, lease, and row version
mark main READY, BLOCKED, or FAILED;
set detected MIME or bounded error_code;
read authorized main and active detail
[accepted result exists with the same payload]
short transaction: lock main and detail;
active detail present, and not expired
referenced_at not null, and matching digest

The private Object Key is exactly attachment_id.
It has no prefix, path, filename, or public URL.
Knowing the ID is not authorization.
Upload retries create a new attachment_id.
Create-only conflict keeps FAILED detail for audited reconciliation
and never overwrites or deletes an object of unproven ownership.
The file body exists only in OBS; openGauss stores metadata.
The permanent main row retains only attachment_id, session_id,
status, created_at, and deleted_at after deletion.
The active detail exists only before DELETED.
referenced_at not null means the Session has referenced the file.
Referenced rows clear expires_at and cannot be deleted alone.
If Runtime persistence later fails, conservative retention lasts
until Session deletion; there is no release protocol.
detected_media_type and expected/actual sizes enforce content policy.
SHA-256 protects upload, scan, proxy, and Runtime integrity.
referenced_at and expires_at govern one-way reference and 24-hour cleanup.
error_code records a bounded safe failure reason.
and row_version provide retry, crash recovery, and race protection.
The WebSocket carries only ordered attachment_ids.
agent-service has no OBS endpoint, credentials, or direct access.
Object Key equality does not widen its authorization.
Runtime history stores exactly attachment_id, filename,
File bodies are untrusted user data.
